# Continuation Critique — Gevurah Against Apparent Completion

The Awtsmoos gives form to light; Awtsmoos.com must give each selector and behavior a bounded vessel.
This pass attacks inherited success so cosmetic completion cannot masquerade as product completion.

## Thirty improvements and traps to test

1. Passing auto-scroll unit tests is insufficient until a real owning element moves.
2. Prove pause by a stable `scrollTop` interval, not merely a status string.
3. Prove resume by renewed measured movement.
4. Prove stop by state and stable movement after enough frames could occur.
5. Change WPM during a run and compare measured velocity.
6. Confirm inner-root selection only when computed overflow and extent prove it scrollable.
7. Confirm natural document fallback on a real route.
8. Build CSS closure from HTML links plus recursive `@import`, never a directory grep alone.
9. Distinguish active historical CSS from dormant history before deletion.
10. Count every active `!important`; the rewritten active system must not depend on it.
11. Find competing fixed-position ownership for rails, settings, menu, comments, and sidebars.
12. Map z-index layers semantically instead of escalating arbitrary numbers.
13. Test hover only on hover-capable input and active feedback on touch.
14. Test `:focus-visible` through keyboard navigation, not source inspection alone.
15. Emulate reduced motion and verify ambient movement actually stops or collapses.
16. Verify safe-area handling at both 390x844 and 430x932.
17. Open every registered Main Menu child and verify return navigation.
18. Ensure dismissal removes invisible interceptors and restores underlying reader access.
19. Ensure Scribe's Lens internal scroll does not drag the underlying reader.
20. Verify every Scribe control changes real state and reset returns production defaults.
21. Trace community errors to the actual server response; never fake an empty state.
22. Verify retry creates a fresh request and can recover after failure.
23. Verify paragraph indexing, especially displayed Para 27 versus transport indexing.
24. Verify heichel, series, post, and alias IDs are correct and URL-safe.
25. Test long English and Hebrew Heichel titles for wrap, direction, and displaced actions.
26. Test Heichel empty/loading/error states, not only happy-state cards.
27. Ensure every social style, including pseudo-elements and media rules, remains beneath `.awtsmoos-social-root`.
28. Inspect profile, composer, notifications, reactions, comments, discovery, search, side rails, and admin-looking surfaces beyond the feed.
29. Review every touched file over 120 lines for safe extraction without shrinking documentation.
30. Search for regressions after each repair because one resolved ownership conflict can reveal another.

## Evidence order

Browser observation > measured DOM state > network/server response > integration test > unit test > static inspection > inference.

## DELTA questions

- Which prior acceptance criteria were never browser-tested?
- Which active imports still carry historical ownership?
- Which user-facing routes were absent from the original plan?
- Which runtime failures predate this pass but are exposed by the redesign?
- Which old compatibility layers are still necessary, and which are merely imported debt?

## NEXT_ACTION

After auto-scroll unit tests, derive the active post CSS closure and route/runtime graph while tracing community transport, then choose only the smallest whole-file rewrites supported by evidence.
